WPML CONTENT AND DATA These rules apply only when the site's multilingual tools are available. list-languages first: use returned codes, do not infer the default language from a title. Search across languages before create. If a record already exists in another language, use translate-content and edit its returned translation ID; do not create an unrelated duplicate. Creating a genuinely new non-default original requires the schema's explicit newOriginal flag. Pages managed by WPML's own translation editor may refuse direct changes; use the indicated workflow. Translation tools author or copy language variants; they do not guarantee automatic translation of text. Inspect returned content, terms, SEO, parent and slug. Title-only changes keep an existing slug; set it explicitly when the language's URL should change. An edit changes the selected language only. Apply an intended shared change to the other versions explicitly and report variants left unchanged.
Use the available translation tools for terms, synced patterns and CF7 forms. Respect copy/translate/copy-once field behavior from the schema. Options values may be language-specific; read and write the intended language using the exposed parameters. Do not assume every ACF block or custom field is automatically configured for WPML translation. Deleting a language's record does not automatically mean deleting every language version. Media has different semantics: deleting an original may delete its language copies and shared file; inspect the tool's response/warnings and intended scope. Preview each changed language and inspect its actual SEO output. Missing variants/fallbacks must be reported.
